assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defining GLP-1 as an incretin and glucagon-like peptide with glucose-dependent insulinotropic, satiety and gastric effects, and converting that physiology into incretin drugs, has transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and is now showing benefit on cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The physiological discovery is clear, original and has very large lasting impact on patients.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and its secretion and actions in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 receptor biology, intestinal GLP-2 and DPP-4 pharmacology) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and its insulinotropic activity) are the most defensible three from the supplied names. Knudsen's drug-development role (liraglutide, semaglutide) is real but is more industrial and translational, so I leave her out of a three-person physiological prize. Credit with Mojsov and others (for example Habener, not on this list) is contested in the literature and I cannot verify the details independently.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drug classes and large randomized outcome trials. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue given clinical scale.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Mojsov, Habener, Holst and Drucker is disputed and I have not independently verified the primary-literature priority.
Whether the committee prefers to honour physiology alone or include the drug-development contribution (Knudsen) is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells carrying chimeric antigen receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemia, lymphoma and myeloma, and are being extended to autoimmune disease including lupus. This is a conceptually new class of living therapy with major lasting clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CD19 CAR with costimulation and preclinical design), June (first clinical proof of durable response in CLL and clinical translation) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and first clinical gene-engineered T cell therapy) form a coherent three-person group from the supplied names. Eshhar and others who made the earliest chimeric receptors are not in the credited list, which weakens a complete attribution.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long follow-up of the first patients. Risks (toxicity, relapse, solid-tumor limits) are known but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: The missing credited name for the earliest chimeric receptor concept complicates the configuration.
Rosenberg's inclusion depends on whether adoptive cell transfer and TIL therapy are viewed as part of the same discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid synovium and that its blockade controls disease established the cytokine-targeted paradigm for chronic inflammatory disease, and anti-TNF therapy has changed outcomes in rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. This is a classic bench-to-bedside discovery with wide and lasting impact. I judge it by the common criteria and not by my own field.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini conceived the TNF hypothesis in rheumatoid arthritis and led the first clinical trials, which is a clear and compact two-person configuration. The supplied credit list does not include those who cloned TNF or developed the antibodies, so the allocation relies on the clinical-translational claim.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty-five years of use, many independent trials and biosimilars. Fully mature and arguably late.
uncertainties: Contributions from TNF biology and antibody engineering outside the supplied names may be seen as part of a larger compound discovery.
It is a clinical translation prize and the committee may weigh this against more mechanistic candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identifying an intronic splicing silencer and designing an antisense oligonucleotide (nusinersen) that corrects SMN2 splicing converted a fatal infantile neurodegenerative disease into a treatable one. It is a clear mechanism-to-therapy case and established a template for splice-modulating RNA drugs.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and the SMN2 target) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are the two decisive contributors in the supplied credit. Others, such as those who identified SMN1 and SMN2 as the disease genes, are not credited here, which leaves attribution partly open.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with growing long-term outcome data and parallel approaches (gene therapy, small molecules) that confirm the SMN target. Timely.
uncertainties: Gene identification for SMA (not in the credit list) may compete for recognition.
Whether the committee sees this as a single discovery or as a broader RNA therapeutics prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defines how cytosolic DNA is sensed and converted to type I interferon and inflammatory responses, and it links infection, cancer immunity, senescence and interferonopathies such as STING-associated vasculopathy and lupus-like disease. As someone aware of the interferon signature in autoimmunity, I regard the conceptual impact as high, applying the common criteria and not field loyalty.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP, and Barber identified STING; these two are the most decisive from the supplied names. Others on the list (Sun, Wu, Ishikawa) made important contributions, especially in Chen's laboratory and in STING characterization, but I favour a compact configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed by structural and genetic work from many groups. Therapeutic translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) is still not established in the clinic, so the clinical impact is not yet proven.
uncertainties: Clinical benefit from pathway modulation is unproven.
Credit for the cGAMP and cGAS discoveries within the Chen group, and the role of Ishikawa in STING, could argue for a different configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identifying BCL11A as a repressor of fetal hemoglobin from human genetic association, and showing that its enhancer can be edited to reactivate fetal hemoglobin, led directly to approved gene-editing therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. It links human genetics, regulatory biology and genome editing in a compact, convincing story.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran established BCL11A as the repressor and its regulation, and Bauer advanced the enhancer-editing strategy that underlies the therapy. Thein's genetic-association work contributes to the fetal hemoglobin story but is more peripheral to the decisive mechanism. The genome-editing tool itself would be recognised separately, since it was already awarded in 2020.
assessment.maturity: First therapy approved in 2023, so patient follow-up is short, though the biology has been confirmed independently. Possibly a little early.
uncertainties: Long-term safety and durability of edited therapies are not yet established.
The relative weight of Thein, Orkin and Sankaran in the genetic-association discovery is not clear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib showed that a selective inhibitor of the causative kinase can produce durable remission in chronic myeloid leukemia, and it established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Sawyers' work on resistance mutations and subsequent inhibitors strengthens the framework.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (drug program and compound development), Druker (clinical proof and trials) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) is a plausible trio. The earlier discoveries of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL (Nowell, Rowley, Groffen, Baltimore and others) are not credited and are partly deceased, which complicates a prize centred on drug development. I am not certain about exactly which chemist should be credited.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of data with high survival. Very mature, with the risk that the prize is seen as lacking a mechanistic core.
uncertainties: Whether the foundational cytogenetic and oncogene discoveries should be recognised alongside the drug.
Role of the medicinal chemist (Zimmermann, not on the list) in the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, and population data now show large declines in cervical disease. This is a major preventive medicine achievement and a decisive complement to the 2008 HPV prize for the causal virus.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity), and Frazer (parallel VLP work and vaccine development) form a plausible group, but the credit with Jian Zhou (deceased) and the Georgetown/Rochester groups is entangled and I cannot independently settle priority.
assessment.maturity: Vaccines have been in use for about two decades with real-world effectiveness data. Mature and timely, with long-term cancer-endpoint data now accumulating.
uncertainties: Priority disputes among the VLP groups and the contribution of a deceased inventor.
Whether the committee considers this sufficiently distinct from the earlier HPV recognition.
